articleTitle: On the Optimal Placement of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Increasing the adoption of Electric Vehicles (EV) is an integral part of many strategies to address climate change and air pollution. However, Electric Vehicle adoption rates are inhibited by several factors which reduces the confidence of potential buyers of electric vehicles, namely range anxiety and limited charging infrastructure. The latter concern can be addressed by carefully planning the placement of Electric Vehicle charging stations to sustainably meet long-term demand. We outline a methodology to optimally allocate Electric Vehicle Charging stations using a novel approach to demand estimation, by first transforming demand using a weighted neighbourhood average and applying a regularised regression. Using this approach the first two authors placed second in the Academic category of an International Shell competition which was created to obtain solutions to this problem. They were also provided with a grant to further study this approach and to develop a deployment strategy.

articleTitle: Identification of fields of action for validation in Systems Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The development of new complex mechatronic systems, especially in the field of special purpose engineering, is characterized by a variety of challenges. These development processes are defined by the strong individuality of each product and specific customer requirements. Systems engineering meets these challenges and provides the basis for the development of a robust system architecture to ensure a reliable product that meets customer requirements despite possible changes. In systems engineering, the validation process must be given special importance to avoid unwanted developments and high costs. Therefore, this paper aims to present the need for an integrative view of the validation process in order to be successful in engineering of complex mechatronic systems. To this end, semi-structured interviews were conducted with twelve experts, which identified three fields of actions that companies in the B2B sector, such as special purpose engineering, need to pay attention to. These fields of action are discussed in detail in this paper and evaluated by domain experts using the example of special purpose engineering.

articleTitle: Personality Prediction from Arabic Text: A Machine Learning Approach for Job Candidate Screening
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Personality prediction from text plays a vital role in understanding individuals and aiding decision-making processes. In this study, we present a comprehensive approach for personality prediction from Arabic text specifically tailored for the domain of job candidate screening. Our model incorporates text preprocessing and the extraction of statistical and linguistic features from text, such as word count, average words per sentence, and TF-IDF representation. The feature set is then reduced using a filter-based feature selection method, , and the vector is fed to a Ridge regressor to predict the Big Five personality traits accurately. We did use our model for job candidate screening. Recruiters can be empowered to make more informed preselections, guided by the insights derived from the prediction of personality traits and the suggestions of candidates who best match the job requirements. This improves the screening efficiency. The experimental results demonstrated the effectiveness of our model and its practical applicability in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: A Cost-Minimization approach to Automobile Insurance Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Motor insurance fraud is the most common type of insurance fraud. It is estimated that while 10% to 20% of all claims are fraudulent [1], 21% to 36% of all motor insurance claims may contain elements of fraudulent activity. Detecting all fraudulent cases is difficult because of the limited human and financial resources businesses have at their disposal. Human resource cost can be reduced by deploying automated systems to detect potential fraud and then having humans do a closer inspection of these cases. We address this issue by applying Machine Learning to fraud detection but, instead of the traditional objective of maximizing detection accuracy, we instead minimize the total cost of detecting fraud. In this way we take into account the savings associated from detecting fraud balanced with the cost of human resources as well as the cost of inconveniencing customers by mistakenly accusing them of fraud. We employed a semi-supervised cost-sensitive learning framework where Isolation Forest detected anomalous cases and weighted logistic regression was used to minimize cost to the business.

articleTitle: Description And Typification Of Low-Code Use Cases In Manufacturing Companies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: As manufacturing companies increasingly embrace digitalization to enhance efficiency and effectiveness, the demand for IT specialists has surged. In response, companies are turning to low-code programming as a solution to alleviate the burden on their IT departments. Through the utilization of low-code tools, domain experts, who may lack IT-specialist credentials yet possess valuable insights and domain-specific knowledge, are empowered to develop applications. However, implementing low-code without proper governance can lead to shadow IT and associated risks, where IT activities operate in the background hidden from official IT management. This paper aims to lay a foundation for elaborating a low-code governance by identifying low-code use cases in manufacturing companies and typifying them. Three types of low-code use cases for manufacturing companies are identified: "Development by Domain Experts," "Development by Domain Experts and IT Specialists," and "Development by IT Specialists." These types provide a basis for designing effective low-code governance principles, enabling responsible and efficient use of low-code development in the manufacturing sector.

articleTitle: Forecasting the Gross Domestic Product using LSTM and ARIMA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This article aims to predict the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) time series using two different methods: a connectionist approach based on self-learning by a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, and a statistical approach based on the Box and Jenkins method, represented by an Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) process. The main objective is to compare the performances of the two approaches in terms of mean squared error (MSE) and determine which method provides more accurate and reliable predictions. Based on the experimental results, the LSTM network outperforms the ARIMA model in predicting the GDP time series. The LSTM network achieved a lower MSE of 0.010 compared to the ARIMA model’s MSE of 0.095. This suggests that the LSTM network achieves better prediction accurcy than the ARIMA model in predicting GDP.

Author Keywords: Economic and Financial Time Series Data

articleTitle: A Cost-Reward Optimization Approach to Bank Loan Approvals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Financial institutions often grapple with revenue losses caused by delinquent customers defaulting on loans or customer rejections due to risk aversion. This paper explores machine learning and optimization methods to address this challenge. The approach involves two key steps which are firstly, to employ a range of machine learning methods to select the best algorithm for predicting customer delinquency, and secondly, to use these results to optimize interest rates, thereby reducing delinquency and risk. This optimization offers both new and existing customers an opportunity to access optimized interest rates, enabling financial institutions to increase revenues while managing risk and delinquency effectively. The models achieved high accuracy, with the top-performing algorithm achieving a F1-score of 0.88 and an ROC of 0.986. Consequently, optimized interest rates led to a 37% reduction in risk and a corresponding increase in returns for a specific customer cohort. In conclusion, this research demonstrates that implementing the proposed method allows financial institutions to profit from approved loans without being overly conservative.

articleTitle: Predicting Agricultural Product Unit Production Using the K-Nearest Neighbors Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper presents a study focused on the analysis of phytosanitary production. The objective is to predict pro-duction per unit, in order to optimize production efficiency, as an essential key in the supply chain. The data for this study encompasses production data, product names, and input param-eters (electricity usage, water consumption, and raw materials), with production as the target variable. The machine learning technique applied for forecasting is the K-Nearest Neighbors regression (KNN-R) algorithm, known for its robust performance, especially on small datasets. This results in a predictive model with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.052 and a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.0057. This research provides valuable insights for agricultural and food companies seeking to improve their production forecasting methods and enhance the efficiency of agricultural product manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: A Reference Process Model for the Evolution of Product Portfolios
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The evolution of product portfolios is driven by constantly changing customer needs and existing competitive pressure. In response, companies often develop new products and include them in their product portfolio: Then, many products are hardly used or not used at all, as the new product replaces its predecessor. This is because products are often a further development of a predecessor product. As a result, the product portfolio becomes larger and larger and comprises many elements. The reason: companies lack a structured process which, like a guide, shows the evolution of product portfolios step by step and brings together the previously established product portfolio with the intended further development of the product portfolio. Against this background, existing process models are examined and aggregated to form a reference process model for product portfolio evolution. This article illustrates the approach and the result.

Author Keywords: Reference Process Model for Evolution of Product Portfolios

articleTitle: Cost Optimization of ERP Project: Practical recommendations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Many companies looking to implement an ERP system encounter difficulty in establishing realistic budgets for both short- and long-term periods. They often underestimate many hidden costs and focus solely on the most visible ones. This study offers practical guidelines and recommendations for practitioners regarding ERP implementation and upgrades. These insights are drawn from existing literature, interviews with ERP consultants, and expert recommendations. During the interviews, participants were questioned about the factors contributing to hidden costs during implementation, as well as strategies for identifying and optimizing these costs. By integrating theoretical insights from the literature with practical findings, six actionable recommendations emerge that can significantly reduce the overall life cycle cost of the project and effectively manage the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO).

articleTitle: Reducing Defects in Garment Manufacturing: A DMAIC Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Quality is the basic ingredient to be added to the product service to make it according to consumer's demand. The Garment manufacturing industries are always in limelight whenever project management, marketing management, control management and management related to the quality of product is concerned. Quality can be seen in a variety of ways. The fundamental line is always defined by customer requirement. This research paper will provide the concept between quality and customer satisfaction by decreasing the defects and increasing the quality of products. Six sigma offers a wide range of tools and capability analysis is one of those tools which are used to keep the company in a state of progress and to assure the standards of the products. Capability indices enable the measurement of the ability and potential of processes in various ways, so the company can choose the optimum way to measure it. If any process contains bias and deviation, then the analysis enables the organization to calculate the level of variation within a process from its mean and how biased the specifications are. Here specifications could be referred to anything like customer demand, international standards, and manufacturing requirements. This project focused on improving the stitching process of basic 5 pocket denim jeans in a renowned garment manufacturing company. Utilizing the Six Sigma DMAIC approach, the project aimed to reduce defect variations and increase overall quality and efficiency. The successful implementation of this structured approach resulted in a more efficient and high-quality stitching process.

articleTitle: How Online Customer Review and Online Customer Rating Influence Customer Purchase Decision on E- Marketplace with Customer Trust as A Mediator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This research aims to determine the influence of online customer reviews and ratings on customer purchase decisions in e-marketplaces through customer trust as a mediator, particularly in the snack industry. The method used in this study is path analysis. This research employs a quantitative method and utilizes purposive sampling technique. The data used is primary data obtained from a survey and gained 150 respondents who have purchased snack products on e-marketplace websites and reside in the Greater Jakarta area. The survey data processing is tested using IBM SPSS Statistic 23 software. The achieved results are used to determine the direct and indirect effects of independent variables on the dependent variable. The research findings concluded that there is a significant influence of online customer reviews and online customer ratings on customer purchase decisions on e-marketplaces through customer trust as a mediating variable.

articleTitle: On the Prediction of Kidney Stone Formers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The early detection of kidney stone formers will significantly reduce treatment costs as well as the discomfort and inconvenience experienced by patients. We collected demographic data, health data and kidney stone information from 1220 individuals. Our objective was to determine how precisely we can predict if an individual will develop a kidney stone in the near future given their demographic and health data. We applied traditional machine learning methods, specifically Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression Support Vector Machine and Perceptron, to perform this task and obtained reasonable results. We then applied a newly developed regression approach that works well on small data sets and found that it outperformed the traditional machine learning approaches. We believe that this new approach can be used to better predict kidney stone formers.

articleTitle: A Method for Automatically Generating CAD Shelf Maps Based on Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Generally, the floorplan of a super store is manually drawn based on the multi-layered CAD shelf maps. This approach is accordingly ineffective, time-consumed, and easily subject to error. This paper presents a method for automatically identifying and localizing objects on CAD shelf maps by imaging processing. To obtain the map characteristics, the CAD file can be initially converted into a pixel based binary image. Features such as cross points, rectangular shape can be identified respectively by line-detection techniques and double-calculation methods with a certain threshold. Through this way, the pixel coordinates, lengths, and widths of all the objects in the image can be determined. The pixel dimensions of the objects can be converted to real-world dimensions by multiplying them with a scaling factor. This method is essential for indoor localization work and can be widely used for different large indoor scenarios such as stores or warehouses.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Student Academic Performance and Analysis of Environmental Change: A Random Forest Regression Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive examination of the Key Stage Examinations, commonly used in St. Lucia and the Caribbean to assess the academic proficiency of elementary school students. Positioned within the realm of Predictive Modelling and Forecasting, the research aims to explore the predictive capabilities of Key Stage Exam 1 and 2 results in relation to Key Stage Exam 3 outcomes. Additionally, the study delves into the influence of environmental factors, specifically exploring the dynamics associated with student transferring, variations in school models and, the impact of school type (public or private) on students’ academic performance. The study aspires to contribute meaningfully to the educational discourse in St. Lucia and the Caribbean at large, establishing a scholarly foundation for understanding the factors that influence students’ academic trajectories, particularly in the context of the environment. Through methodological rigor, analytical examination, and the use of Random Forest Regression, this research seeks to make a valuable contribution to the existing body of knowledge in the domain of educational assessment and predictive modelling.

articleTitle: Exploratory study on adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Ireland: A Comprehensive Review of Barriers and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Industry 4.0 represents a comprehensive digital transformation in the way companies operate, incorporating advanced technologies. While Industry 4.0 and similar technologies have many conceivable benefits for manufacturing, most of these technologies are developed for or by large companies. This article proposes to investigate the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Ireland, exploring the challenges faced by these companies and identifying the potential opportunities arising from this adoption. An exploratory systematic review of the literature was made. In total, 43 studies satisfied the screening and selection criteria. The consolidated factors were grouped into categories to help understand the challenges faced by small and medium-sized companies in the transition to Industry 4.0 in Ireland. This research observed several barriers for SMEs, but also identified numerous opportunities related to Industry 4.0. The main barriers analyzed in Ireland are organizational and technical barriers and the main opportunities are associated with horizontal and vertical integration opportunities.

articleTitle: Enhancing Transportation Mode Prediction from GPS Trajectories using Machine Learning and Feature Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This manuscript proposes a comprehensive framework for the automated determination of travel modes based solely on GPS trajectories. To improve prediction accuracy, additional preprocessing features are introduced, including speed, acceleration, jerk, and bearing rate. Our approach employs various machine learning techniques, such as Random Forest, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), AdaBoost Classifier, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), to achieve notable classification results. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our framework surpasses existing state-of-the-art algorithms for transport mode prediction. This investigation presents a promising approach for accurate and reliable prediction of travel modes, with potential applications in various real-world scenarios..

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Elderly Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The present paper present a bibliometric analysis on the actual research interest on the use and application of Artificial Intelligence systems to the different need of elderly in the field of business and management. The Elderly population is a now a Grand Challenge, the United Nation declared the next decade as the decade of healthy ageing we would analyze what is the actual research interest on the use and applications of Artificial Intelligence systems to the different need of elderly and how are the emerging themes that could allow to arrive to an Elderly Intelligence Management.

articleTitle: Study of Measuring Motor Function in Dementia by Tapping Task Using IoT and Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Dementia has emerged as a significant issue in contemporary Japanese society. Assessing finger motor function is pivotal for diagnosing and rehabilitating individuals with dementia. In this study, we design a web application to gauge manual dexterity through tapping exercises. Our fundamental concept combines finger identification using a web camera and tactile panel input to quantify finger actions. In our proposed methodology, we amalgamate real-time visuals captured by a web camera into the hand.js module within the MediaPipe framework, autonomously generating 21 critical finger data points. Concurrently, we establish touch panel control buttons on the web interface. In the context of the operating interface, participants manipulate their fingers in sync with numbers or features displayed every two seconds and utilize touch panel input to log button presses. This approach facilitates an all-encompassing assessment of finger motor aptitude.

articleTitle: Optimization of Long-Term Profit when Cross-Selling Insurance Policies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Insurance companies try to maximize profits from their existing customers by cross-selling other policies to them. These recommended policies may either be chosen by agents, who may try to maximize commissions, or the company who wants to maximize profit. However, in either case, these policies may not be the most suitable for the client and they may end up either taking the policy but then cancelling or, if it is obviously unsuitable, the customer may cancel all policies and switch to a competitor. In this paper, we aim at reducing these risks of cancellation and dissatisfaction while achieving an acceptable profit. To achieve this, we propose and apply benefit-based decision trees to predict customer satisfaction and their probability of cancellation if offered a given policy. These trees are trained with the goal of maximizing long term profits. Long term profits are achieved when the client purchases a profitable policy but does not cancel due to dissatisfaction. An overall score is calculated using suitability predictions, cancellation probability and long term benefits of the policies. The policy with the highest score is recommended to the client. We demonstrate the benefit of our approach using data from an insurance company.

articleTitle: A Logistic Provider - Threat Evaluation and Weapon Selection using Analytical Hierarchy Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Air Defense is the basic nation’s need for the sovereignty and defense of the homeland. Numerous studies have been conducted to improve the efficiency of threat evaluation and weapon assignment (TEWA), but still improvement is required in terms of time and cost. The weapon assignment is done during the wartime, but in stressed situation, errors may get occurred while assigning the appropriate weapon to neutralize threats. Assigning an erroneous weapon without having the ability to hit target at a certain height and speed would result in catastrophic consequences. Use of correct weapon for the target is always remained a goal for all decision-makers. The weapon is selected based on the evaluation of threats considering its significant parameters. This paper proposes a weapon selection model using Analytical Hierarchy Approach (AHP) to assist decision-makers in the efficient use of resources by selecting effective and efficient weapon in terms of time and cost. The results show that significant results can be achieved with the proposed model.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Feature Encoding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Target based encoding is a feature encoding technique that replaces categorical values with the mean of the target variable for each category. This can be done for both classification and regression problems. In this paper, we propose a novel target encoding method that can be used for categorical as well as continuous data. We evaluate our novel approach, referred to as kappa (κ) encoding, in regression problems with a series of data types. The approach is robust and shows significant improvement over a series of Machine Learning Regressors. We demonstrate that our proposed method has the potential to improve the performance of Machine Learning models on a variety of regression tasks.

articleTitle: Boolean Programming for Optimal Stopping in American Option Pricing with Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the effective implementation of Reinforcement Learning for American Option Pricing. We treat American Option Pricing problems as Optimal Stopping Problems and apply Monte-Carlo Simulation. We solve the Stopping problems in American Option Pricing using Q-Learning and Reinforcement Learning. We analyze the details of Function Approximation and treat the Stopping Problem with Boolean Programming. By applying Boolean Programming, the problem can be treated with convex optimization, making the numerical algorithms more efficient. We conduct Numerical Experiments using the codes developed in the references using Matlab and Python. Through simulation experiments using our approaches of Reinforcement Learning and Boolean Programming, we obtain good results in finding solutions for Optimal Stopping in American Options Pricing.

articleTitle: MLOps: Creating powerful AI pipelines by stitching together heterogeneous Machine Learning models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: As Machine Learning and Deep Learning are being widely adopted in different industries, in many cases there is also a need to use these models together to have a system or a solution that is capable of performing much better on a task than the individual models can. Or even perform tasks that the individual models cannot perform by themselves in isolation. We developed the Acumos AI Platform that provides capabilities to create powerful AI pipelines by stitching together heterogeneous Machine Learning models. We will demonstrate with multiple examples how we can create such powerful AI pipelines which we will call ‘composite ML solutions’ using the Acumos Design Studio. We will use some other components we developed i.e. Acumos Runtime Orchestrator, proto viewer, Data broker, Splitter, and Collator to deploy the aforementioned composite ML solutions as a set of communicating microservices. The individual ML models that are part of the composite solution may not necessarily have been created by the same person or same group or the same organization or have been created in a particular language or use a particular ML framework. But still, Acumos allows these models created in disparate languages and frameworks by different individuals or organizations to be stitched (subject to their compatibility) together to create composite solutions using a simple intuitive GUI and deploy them very easily to various cloud targets. In this paper, we will describe these novel capabilities that we have developed in Acumos and we will show how to create and deploy a composite ML solution or an AI pipeline using this toolset.

articleTitle: Audit in the Era of Big Data and Blockchain Technology, What Implications?
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The current society is constantly evolving. Today, one of the main trends impacting the world is digitization. Organizations are also affected by waves of digitalization. In order to meet the ever-changing and accelerating customer demand, they must leverage these technologies to adapt their way of working. These technologies will enable them to be more efficient. The purpose of this study is to get a greater comprehension of the technologies that impact the audit profession. The study focused on exploring the effects of big data and blockchain technology on the audit profession via semi-directed interviews with selected auditors from different audit companies. The insights gained from the interviews expanded the understanding of big data and blockchain within the audit field. The study revealed four main themes that were consistent with the participants feedback regarding the impact of big data and blockchain on auditing. These four fields are: 1 devotion to training personnel in new audit software and methodologies, 2 need for IT support to assist technological knowledge gaps among auditors, 3 adoption of specific audit software apart from Excel in organizations, 4 limited experience or early-stage adoption of big data and blockchain in audit firms. The study's findings can be useful for auditors and other collaborators who aim to work with customers that use technologies in their systems.

articleTitle: A Review of Assembly Line Balancing Heuristics and Value Stream Mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Value stream mapping (VSM) and assembly line balancing heuristics are widely used in manufacturing and operations management. Value stream mapping aims to reduce wastage in the production process, while assembly line balancing optimizes task and resource distribution. Assembly line balancing heuristics employ algorithms like largest candidate rule, ranked positional weight rule, and Kilbridge and Wester technique to enhance output, cut costs, and improve efficiency. VSM visualizes the entire production process to identify and eliminate non-value-added activities, leading to process improvement, reduced lead times, optimized inventory, and increased customer satisfaction. Both techniques complement each other, with assembly line balancing heuristics focusing on the assembly line's flow and value stream mapping considering the entire manufacturing process, leading to better overall operations.

articleTitle: Review of Risk Identification within Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) Projects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Throughout their lifespan, proj ects are constantly exposed to risks and opportunities; risk management is one of the factors that contributes to project success, particularly in Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) proj ects. Risks can come from several different places, including a lack of funding, unforeseen circumstances, strategic mistakes, etc. The first crucial step in effective risk management is the identification and evaluation of risks. However, EPC projects are well-known for their complexity, which makes managing and controlling them with absolute certainty challenging. Consequently, these projects are often characterized by uncertainty, especially in their early stages. To increase the likelihood of successful project completion and mitigate the effects of uncertainty, it is essential to identify and manage risks properly. This study's purpose is to present a systematic review of literature on risk assessment in EPC proj ects, identify common risks and establish criteria for prioritizing risks. The methodology includes analysing databases like Taylor & Francis, Science Direct, and Emerald, along with interviews with project managers to define relevant criteria.

articleTitle: Improving Academic Advising by Predicting a Student’s GPA given their Chosen Courses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The academic advising process is very beneficial since many students are unaware of the difficulties they may face when taking certain courses or combinations of courses in the upcoming semester. Unfortunately, it is difficult for academic staff to take into account the various factors that may affect the student’s performance given their choice of courses. We believe that historical student data can assist with this task. One can use tools such as collaborative filtering to predict the performance of a student on a set of courses given the past performances of similar students as well as the past performance of the individual. An academic advisor can then use this information to provide better advice to the student to avoid course over-loading or even course under-loading. We present one such approach in which, given a set of courses for the coming semester, we predict the semester GPA of the student if they were to take these courses. Through this advice the student may then decide to reduce their course load in order to maintain a high grade point average or increase their course load to complete their degree earlier. We use data from a Computer Science department at a University and demonstrate that, using the available demographic and course grade data, one can make reasonably accurate predictions to assist the advisor.

articleTitle: Distance Learning and Students’ Problem-Solving Ability: Case Study of Hassan First University
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The study aims at providing insights, by way of a case study, into the effect internal and external factors have on students’ developing problem-solving ability in distance learning. Using data collected through surveying 103 students enrolled in a SPOC designed particularly for Management students, a binary logistic regression is performed to assess the relationship between the specified variables. The results of the regression show that students’ commitment has a positive effect on them acquiring problem-solving ability. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that encouraging students to make suggestions and taking into consideration their reactions affect positively their ability to solve problems in an online education. In addition, the findings indicate that students using desktop computers in online learning have a higher chance of developing problem- solving ability. Conversely, students who use tablets are less likely to acquire this ability. Finally, the results show that students getting help from their teachers with technical problems are more likely to develop problem-solving abilities.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Cultural Heritage Ontologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Currently, the amount of heterogeneous data on cultural heritage is constantly increasing. The use of ontologies provides an effective formalism to overcome obstacles related to data integration problems and facilitates good knowledge management. As a result, the number of ontologies in the field of cultural heritage has increased rapidly. With this development, the structure and design of ontologies become increasingly complex. The evaluation of ontologies becomes essential for the construction or reuse of ontologies. During the process of building ontologies, evaluation is beneficial for both users and developers. According to the case study, this evaluation will allow them to select the optimal ontology among the candidate ontologies. This work proposes an evaluation process for cultural heritage ontologies that takes into consideration the evaluation of the quantity, structure, and design of the ontology. The evaluation process is based on Base, Graph, Schema, and Density metrics. We have proposed a formula for calculating density that proves its effectiveness in determining the most adequate ontology in the studied domain. For instance, we obtained Cidoc as a result in the Top-level ontology category, and in the Bibliographic Information sub-category, FRBRoo was identified.

articleTitle: Oracle Trust Models for Blockchain-Based Applications. An early standardization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Blockchain, as a disruptive technology, opened the gate to a wave of potential innovations. However, despite the rapidly growing load of hype, recent research shows that integration into the business, apart from a few applications, is coming at a slower rate. One reason for that delay may be the need in real-world applications for a working "trust model." Trust models are rarely mentioned in blockchain application proposals despite their importance, which creates skepticism about their successful developments. To date, there is still no standard or preferred way to implement a trust model, making auditing the related project more challenging. To contribute to blockchain trust model research and their standardization, this article provides an adaptable trust model framework tested on an already operating blockchain integration. Outlining the integration features and criticalities, the redacted trust model can help managers improve the blockchain application and other stakeholders to evaluate its potential.

articleTitle: Investigating the potential of artificial intelligence for the employee from the perspective of AI-experts
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has developed rapidly in recent months. In the form of chatbots, texting is becoming easier in our everyday lives. The potential for using this technology in industry is also growing. Small and medium-sized companies, in particular, are still underutilizing the opportunity to use AI in production and development as a competitive advantage or for sustainability goals. People are also often neglected in the introduction of new technologies. From a socio-technical perspective, employees must be explicitly considered as active co-creators and users of AI, whose knowledge of work processes and interactions with technology enriches the design of the human-technology interface and, in the long run, the development of the technology itself. This paper examines how employees have used AI in the past, what their requirements are for their work and collaboration processes, and how they view the possibilities of technologies such as AI. Using a predominantly qualitative approach, this paper describes the socio-technical aspects that companies need to consider. The findings are consistent with previous literature and have been validated in expert workshops. This forms the basis for helping companies to develop this technology for themselves.

articleTitle: State of the Art and Themes of the Research on Artificial intelligence (AI) Integrated Customer Relationship Management (CRM): Bibliometric Analysis and Topic Modelling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: By integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Customer Relationship Management (CRM), businesses can enhance customer engagement and streamline operations. Rapid advancements in AI along with the digital shift triggered by the COVID-19 pandemic have created a surge in AI-CRM research. Yet a comprehensive review of this burgeoning field remains elusive. The purpose of our study is to bridge this gap by providing insights into the evolution and thematic landscape of the field of AI-CRM research. Through the application of bibliometric and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling techniques, we reviewed 810 articles from the past two decades, identifying seven predominant themes that encompass the trajectory of research in AI-CRM.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impacts of Digital Anti-Corruption Tools in Moroccan Public Administrations: An Exploratory Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The fight against corruption is crucial for Public Administrative Organizations (PAOs). Hence, the implementation of Digital Anti-corruption Tools (DATs) has become one of the priorities for governance in the public sector. The aim of the paper is to provide an exploratory case study of the multiple impacts of DATs used in the Moroccan PAO context. Via a logical framework approach, a method used in project management systems for planning projects and evaluating them, this paper provides an assessment of the multifaceted effects of DATs in the Moroccan context. It applies a mixed-methods approach based on three tasks that integrate with each other. The results provide a summary of the main findings regarding the outcomes generated by the introduction of new DAT initiatives. Finally, this paper provides insights into the most impactful DATs used in the Moroccan context.

articleTitle: Digital Technology for Natyashastra’s "Rasa" Measurement to Interpret Online Learning Engagement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Determining learners' engagement has become challenging as virtual learning platforms' rapid adaptation for training has increased. Face-to-face learning was believed to be an effective way to understand learners' participation, emotions, behavior, and transfer of knowledge, concepts, innovation, etc. as a mindful engagement; however, now virtual technologies have been shown to be fast and effective in context, transforming our world into an excellent learning resource. This paper introduces the My Learning Engagement Assessment Framework (My-LEAF), a digital tool based on the Rasa theory of Indian Natyashastra (Theatrical Science). This digital tool measures Rasas prescribed in Natyashastra and interprets learner learning engagement (LLE) in online learning platforms with an emphasis on learner ownership to enhance mindful engagement. The latest technology-enabled My-LEAF tool can support the learning and development (L&D) domain for LLE. The aim of the study is to explore the digital application of an ancient Vedic expression-based emotions capturing scientific theory to interpret and measure engagement as a moderator for learner ownership. The mixed research method involved 25 learners for My-LEAF tool experimentation. The results revealed that My LEAF, a Rasa-based LLE measurement digital tool score, has a significant correlation with assessment-based learning engagement scores. Thus, digital technology-enabled Rasa measurement can support the virtual learning platforms to improve LLE and learning ownership, thereby contributing to the L&D domain by enhancing knowledge management and innovation.

articleTitle: Assessment of The Healthcare Providers' Acceptance of Telemedicine: Case of Endocrinology Teleclinics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: In recent years, patients’ encounters have shifted to virtual visits and remote assessments due to the crisis caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Thus, this study aimed to assess the healthcare providers adoption and acceptance of the teleclinic services using qualitative methodology. Interviews with care providers were conducted to evaluate provider’s experience and measure teleclinics' success in order to develop the used tools and enhance the provided services. In this study, multiple factors were chosen from different very well-known technology acceptance models, such as UTAUT, TAM, TTF, TPB, TRA, and other model factors, to comprehend more indicators. This study aims to enhance the understanding of the factors that play an important role in the success of teleclinics and should help healthcare organizations maximize the benefits of such tools. Findings suggest that digital literacy, trust, ease of use, and usefulness are very important indicators of adoption and acceptance.

articleTitle: Towards a process framework to guide the development of outcome-based models in a healthcare context
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Africa is challenged with impoverished and ineffective healthcare systems, and despite rampantly increasing healthcare costs, patient outcomes are often unsatisfactory. Outcome-based models (OBMs) improve healthcare spending and outcomes by ensuring that only products and services that perform well and achieve the desired outcomes are paid for with a focus on value rather than volume. However, the implementation of OBMs is complex, and without a comprehensive framework to guide the development of OBMs, the implementation of OBMs becomes constrained. This study builds on five key OBM concepts towards a conceptual framework that is meant to aid the development of OBMs.

articleTitle: Factors affecting Moroccan Citizens’ intention to use E-Government Services – A Measurement Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Morocco, which is undergoing rapid socioeconomic development is facing challenges in implementing online administration systems. Factors such as technological advancements, government regulations, user behavior, and socio-economic constraints affect the quality and utilization of these services. This research examines factors influencing citizens' intention to use e-services in Morocco using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), considering perceived utility, ease of use, intention of use, social influence, user satisfaction, and trust.To design a standardized measurement tool for e-government (E-Gov) services adoption, an exploratory analysis approach was adopted. Based on the analysis of a survey dataset collected from 44 citizens using e-gov services, it can be advocated that the construct validity and internal consistency are both highly satisfactory for the variables examined.

articleTitle: Business strategy taxonomy and solution patterns for the circular economy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The increasing importance of sustainable development confronts companies with various disruptive challenges. It requires them to design their products with environmental considerations, such as reducing emissions, in mind. In this context, the circular economy has emerged as a promising approach. However, a comprehensive transformation of the existing business is required to comply with the principles of the circular economy. Undertaking the circular transformation in a structured and systematic way requires defining the envisioned strategic positioning of the company first. However, companies lack concrete design knowledge on the aspects necessary for strategic positioning in the circular economy. Therefore, this paper aims to develop a holistic taxonomy for describing circular business strategies and suitable solution patterns. A design science approach was chosen as the overarching research approach that orchestrates the research methods for taxonomy and pattern development. The resulting taxonomy for business strategies comprises ten dimensions, such as product design or take-back system, with 31 characteristics. Based on the taxonomy, appropriate solution patterns representing a thrust for strategic positioning in the circular economy were derived. The results enable companies to integrate circular transformation into their strategic planning early.

articleTitle: Coffee as a Service: Embedding Efficiency and Sustainability in Coffee Roasters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This article addresses the issue of sustainability in coffee through a different lens, taking a diametrically opposite approach to cracking the problem compared to the methods adopted so far, by engaging not with producers but with the strongest players at the other side of the value chain, coffee roasters. First, the article provides an unbiased review of sustainability in coffee that is in stark contrast to the dominant discourse and the marketing claims that abound in the industry. Second, it describes the new Coffee as a Service model proposed by a young tech startup that is pioneering transparency and digitalization of the coffee value chain. The proposed solution is rooted in technology and permits to improve the economic efficiency of coffee roasters, while at the same time increasing their transparency and accountability within the value chain. The ambition of this paper is to become, through the startup-led proof of concept, the trigger to a better, more balanced and more redistributive coffee industry, creating momentum towards a more impactful and sustainable coffee sector.

articleTitle: Enhancing QoS in IoT through Big Data-Driven Networking and Computing Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a transformative paradigm, enabling seamless connectivity among a vast array of intelligent devices. However, the exponential growth of connected things has led to increased strain on communication networks and processing mechanisms, subsequently impacting the Quality of Service (QoS) experienced by end-users. In this paper, we explore the significance of IoT and Big Data and their intertwined relationship. We present a comprehensive analysis of IoT’s QoS, which comprises three critical dimensions - QoS object, QoS communication, and QoS computing. To mitigate the challenges posed by burgeoning IoT deployments, we propose leveraging Big Data techniques for the adaptive management of these QoS dimensions. By harnessing Big Data analytics, we aim to optimize the performance and efficiency of IoT networks and computing infrastructure. Our research highlights the vital role of data-driven strategies in sustaining reliable and high-performing IoT ecosystems, ultimately fostering seamless interconnectivity between intelligent devices and improving overall user experience.

articleTitle: Adaptive Learning Systems: A Comprehensive Overview and Identification of Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper examines the challenges of adaptive learning through an in-depth analysis of 16 literature reviews covering the period from 2018 to 2023. It explores different components of adaptive learning systems, highlighting specific challenges related to learner modeling, content design, adaptive technologies and research methodology. Through a detailed examination of these challenges, the article puts forth theoretical and practical solutions. The findings provide valuable insights for the advancement of adaptive learning, offering guidance to enhance learning effectiveness.

articleTitle: Confirmatory factor analysis of individual perception towards peer-to-peer lending platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: As Fintech innovation continues to dominate the financial industry, peer-to-peer lending platforms emerged and are adopted in several countries including Malaysia. This digital lending platform aids Micro, small and medium enterprises to obtain funds with less efforts hence, experiencing a constant growth in Malaysia. Despite the growth, a lot is unknown including investors perception towards the platforms hence, this paper seeks to confirm factors that may constitute investors perception towards peer-to-peer lending platforms. Data was collected for 20 predetermined items based on previous studies in conjunction with the theory of planned behavior. Result indicates that 17 of these items are valid and reliable to measure individual perception towards peer-to-peer lending platforms. In addition, structural equation models indicate a positive relationship between peer-to-peer lending platform awareness, digital financial risks awareness and time pressure on investors’ perceptions towards P2P LP, and perceived risk has no connection. These findings are useful for further studies, and to enhance platform lending operations when consolidating these factors in the lending process.

articleTitle: Analysis of Gartner’s BI&A Capabilities Reports Over a Decade: A Systematic Review Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper aims to provide a comprehensive summary of available data on the capabilities of Business Intelligence and Analytics Platforms (BI&A) from Gartner’s Magic Quadrant reports. A total of 11 reports published between 2012 and 2022 were selected for analysis. The analysis of the data was conducted through the lens of scientific research and the current state of knowledge in the field of BI&A. The data were primarily processed and structured in a database using Excel, and Power BI was also utilized for data analysis. As all the reports met the same eligibility criteria, they were all included in the systematic review.The findings of the study present the research methods used, the categories of capabilities examined, and the key factors considered in studying BI&A capabilities. Additionally, the review identified key trends in critical capabilities of BI&A and the market trends driving the shift from traditional BI to modern BI, which focuses on a broader range of users, combination of two Mode of analytics and enhances the decision-making process. The review also highlights areas that have garnered more attention from vendors. Furthermore, this study suggests potential paths for researchers and practitioners, that can help organizations derive value from BI&A systems through a comprehensive assessment of BI&A capabilities.

articleTitle: A novel data transformation approach for improved cluster performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: We compare the performance of a new feature scaling approach against conventional feature scaling techniques for clustering. Our approach creates a more well-defined cluster structure using a robust weighted average that incorporates the influence of distance between sample points. We show with empirical evaluation metrics that our approach leads to the formation of better-quality clusters. This is demonstrated across multiple datasets and metrics.

articleTitle: Recursive vs. Direct Forecasting of Crop Prices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Food security has become a high priority for many countries after the logistics issues caused by Covid and presently because of issues due to war. External factors can cause crop price fluctuations which can negatively affect farmers financially and emotionally. Our objective is to develop statistical time series forecasting models to predict the future prices of ten crops: tomato, banana, orange, ginger, hot pepper, lettuce, pumpkin, cabbage, cucumber and cassava. Variations of the Seasonal AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average with exogenous factors (SARIMAX) were used with the external variables, volume traded, precipitation and maximum and minimum temperatures. To improve forecasting accuracy, the recursive, direct and DirRec forecasting strategies were compared. In eight instances, for multi-step forecasting, the direct strategy performed best. One-step forecasting was also performed and compared with the Naïve Seasonal Mean Model. The recursive one-step forecasts outperformed the Naïve Seasonal forecasts in seven instances.

articleTitle: The Moderating Effect of Design-Engineering Capability on the Relationship between Firms' Innovation Activity and Financial Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The integration of design and technology innovations in the new product development (NPD) process is critical for successful product development and market success. Technology innovation serves as the backbone of the development side of NPD, empowering products with the necessary functionalities and capabilities. Design innovation, on the other hand, is instrumental in aligning the products with customer needs and preferences, serving as a key driver on the market side of NPD. The present study aims to examine the effects of firms' capability in effectively integrating design and technology throughout the NPD process, which we refer to as design-engineering capability, on financial performance, as well as its moderating effect on the relationship between firms' innovation activity and financial performance. Our main hypothesis is that firms' design-engineering capability positively moderates the effects of innovation activities on financial performance. Using patent data for 1,659 US-headquartered publicly-traded firms from 1980 to 2015, the results of panel generalized least square (GLS) regressions confirm our hypotheses on the direct effect of design-engineering capability on firm performance and its moderating effect on the relationship between innovation activity and firm performance, highlighting the importance of having a strong integration of design and technology expertise within the organization.

articleTitle: Blockchain technology in the Greek Supply Chain sector: An empirical examination of adoption patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of blockchain technology within the Greek supply chain sector, delineating both its potential advantages and accompanying challenges. A quantitative survey was executed, collecting data from participants engaged in the Greek supply chain sector via structured questionnaires. Through non-parametric tests, it was revealed that certain "independent" variables exert a significant influence on the perceived benefits and challenges associated with the adoption of blockchain technology in the Greek logistics sector. For example, long-standing companies in the sector experience technological, organizational, and financial challenges, often stemming from adapting to new technologies or deep-rooted processes. However, these businesses, especially those larger in scale or advanced in blockchain integration, also see significant benefits from the technology. The findings lay the groundwork for future research, which may include comparative studies examining the impact of blockchain technology across distinct sectors such as supply chain and retail.

articleTitle: Implementing AI in HRM: Leveraging Machine Learning for Smart Recruitment Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Resume-Efficient candidate selection has long been a priority for recruiters and businesses, driven by the need to reduce costs and streamline the hiring process. The accuracy of predictive models crucially hinges on the selection of discriminant va-riables, which significantly impact candidate assess-ment. In response, this study focuses on enhancing job performance prediction systems using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models, all optimized through Sequential Forward Selection (SFS). Leveraging his-torical employee data and conditions, this system improves recruitment screening in a four-stage process encompassing data collection, preprocessing, model development, optimization and evaluation. Our comprehensive study compares the performance of each model, providing valuable insights for practitioners and researchers alike, emphasizing the pivotal role of AI and machine learning in human resource manage-ment.

articleTitle: Growth Models for Women-Led Startups: A Structured Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper aims to analyze the literature on female-led startups and their growth paths. A Structured Literature Review (SLR) methodology underpins the research by analyzing 195 research sources. The main findings suggest that since 2012 there has been a considerable increase in the literature on female startups; nevertheless, there are still important gaps to fill in, namely the lack of specific growth models employed by these firms. The research focuses on four major themes: women's empowerment, obstacles to growth, growth archetypes, and SMEs development. Emphasis was placed on presenting growth models adapted to startups led by women. Finally, this research work offers material insights into handling contemporary startup challenges and learning from tactics used in the female sector.

articleTitle: Digital Transformation: Approaches and Perspectives in Latin America. A Systematic Review of the Literature 2012 - 2022
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This research was conducted with the aim of compiling and updating the available information on Digital Transformation, in order to provide relevant academic material for future research. The main objective was to analyse theoretical and empirical studies on the perspectives of different authors in Latin America during the last decade, formulating the following question: What is known about the digital transformation in companies in all sectors in Latin America in the last 10 years? Therefore, a search for scientific articles was carried out in different reliable databases, obtaining a total of 397,477 articles, 87 of which were downloaded and 50 were subsequently selected (18 in Scopus, 10 in Ebsco, 10 in Proquest, 03 in Redalyc, 07 in Scielo and 02 in Dialnet). Thus, after analysing the collected literature, different approaches were found, such as: economics, finance, business, industry, education, communications, digitisation and technology. Its positive impact on companies in all sectors in Latin America is evident, as it provides time optimisation in different processes, and improvements in management and quality. Therefore, it will be essential for companies to continue adapting to the coming changes, given that the Digital Transformation will continue to evolve.

articleTitle: New Digital Technologies In Supply Chain Risk Management: Empirical Results Of Vietnam’s Textile Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Textile industry plays an important role to Vietnam's economy. In 2022, Vietnam's export in terms of textile such as fabrics, cotton, yarns, garments, clothing … was ranked the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> position in the world, just after China and Bangladesh. However, in an ever-changing world, and in the context of the 4.0 revolution, all enterprises in the textile supply chain have been facing a lot of risks both from macro and micro environment. The aim described in this study is fourfold: i) Firstly, do literature review on application of digital technologies for supply chain risk management; ii) investigate authentically risks that textile enterprises in Vietnam are facing; iii) study status quo on application of digital technologies for risk management and finally iv) give suggestions for managing supply chain risks efficiently. For literature review, bibliometric analysis was also employed with the support of VOSviewer software tool in order to explore prominent research clusters. To capture the current status of supply chain risk management and application of digital technologies in Vietnam, the study used snowball sampling method for collecting questionnaires from 30 textile enterprises, combining 4 in-depth interviews to typical enterprises; then the data was analyzed by statistical method and comparison. Results show "Market requirements transformation"; "Competition, competitiveness" and "Uncontrollable external risks" were evaluated as the top risks. Moreover, even though the role of application of digital technologies for supply chain risk management is highly appreciated, most enterprises have a rather modest level of application of digital technologies. Based on these empirical results, suggestions were given for promoting risk management capacity, contributing towards sustainable textile supply chain.

articleTitle: The HR function in Morocco between Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence: Reality and challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The digital revolution has pushed companies to rethink their model, processes, and strategies. However, it was just a first step towards a transformation of work practices, as organizations' focus is now on Artificial Intelligence. In this regard, we conducted an exploratory qualitative study to understand the positioning of the HR function in Morocco, between Digitization and Artificial Intelligence, through the analysis of four HR dimensions: recruitment, training, performance management, and compensation within twelve organizations. The results of our study show that Digitalization is now well-established within the HR function in these firms. However, the deployment of AI remains in its early stages, even though HR managers are open to future adoption of this new technology. For the moment, they face challenges such as change management, ethical considerations, and the need to possess adequate skills.

articleTitle: An investigation of the effect of supply chain digitalization and sustainability on food security through improved forecasting capabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated supply chain disruptions have affected food supply chains (FSCs) globally, sparking interest among experts, practitioners, and decision-makers worldwide. In addition, studies have highlighted that digital technologies (DT) can help improve supply chain disruption through effective forecasting. This research focuses on the impact of digital technology capabilities (DTC) in managing the FSCs in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Thus, how FSC management strategies are used and how they relate to food security (FS), resilience, and sustainability of supply chains. Furthermore, it aims to understand the relationship between the use of DT in various FSCs and their effect on corporate performance. The proposed research hypotheses aim to explain the influence and the mediating relationship of DTC and adaptive forecasting capabilities on the sustainable food system, supply chain resilience, and cooperation in the FSC, in addition to the impact of the firm’s profits on the sustainable food system. Through a survey, the research study will aim to address the presented research questions. One of the most significant gaps was the paucity of studies on FSC sustainability using DTC in the UAE. The study will also provide valuable insights into the implementation and use of DTs in the FSCs to reduce food loss and improve the ability to predict and track food through real-time information exchange.

articleTitle: Decrypting Disruptive Technologies: Review and Research Agenda of Explainable AI as a Game Changer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has completely disrupted the entirety of the modern life. For researchers in computer science, AI experts, and professionals in a variety of fields, AI is nowadays an intriguing subject of study. However, leveraging AI techniques exposes users to potential risks as these techniques ordinarily function as black boxes, making users prey to inappropriate modeling methods as well as biased decision-making. To address this issue, the key objective of Explainable AI (XAI) frameworks is to render systems’ decisions comprehensible to the users so as to make them trustworthy and dependable. With the goal to present an extensive overview, this systematic review attempts to incorporate the majority of the XAI literature. A framework-based review of 122 articles was performed to accomplish this using the TCM-ADO framework (Theory, Context, Methods and Antecedents, Decision, Outcomes). The study further seeks to accentuate the significant gaps in the literature and offer specific recommendations for further research. These results and recommendations can be used by researchers in the fields of computer science, social sciences and others. By displacing the existing black-box AI with XAI, the integration of XAI into modern businesses has the ability to bring about social transformation by radically altering people’s perceptions of AI.

articleTitle: Transforming Advertising: Harnessing AI for Personalised Customer-Centricity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: In the era of customer-centricity, customers are flooded with information. This leads to a time-consuming, frustrating and overwhelming process of finding the ideal product. The use of traditional advertising methods is not enough to make the customer journey personalised and effective. For an organisation to be advantageous in the current scenario, it must target the right customers at the right time with the right proposition. The development and usage of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in advertising is, in effect, to leverage the pool of customer information to transform advertising. This study investigates the pivotal role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in reshaping advertising, with a primary focus on personalised customer-centricity. This research aims to elucidate how AI can be effectively leveraged to revolutionise advertising practices, ensuring that the right message reaches the right audience at the right time. Our methodology involves a comprehensive review of relevant literature and an analysis of real-world case studies across diverse industries and advertising platforms. Through this approach, we uncover compelling findings that underscore the transformative potential of AI in advertising. It is evident that Businesses that embrace AI-driven personalisation witness enhanced customer engagement but also experience substantial improvements in advertising return on investment (ROI). This shift towards AI-optimised advertising yields increased sales, heightened customer loyalty, and improved brand perception. Moreover, it enables precise targeting, resulting in enhanced cost-effectiveness. The implications of this study are far-reaching. Organisations are encouraged to invest in AI technologies to harness customer data effectively, delivering tailored advertising experiences. However, ethical considerations and transparency in data handling remain paramount. This research serves as a clarion call for businesses to stay at the forefront of AI advancements, fostering a culture of innovation to remain competitive and customer-centric in the ever-evolving advertising landscape.

articleTitle: The Effect of Incentive Mechanism on Knowledge Transfer Network: An Agent-Based Model Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Knowledge transfer plays a vital role in the growth and sustainability of organizations. It also creates opportunities for employees to work together and share ideas which are helpful for their professional development. Organizations can keep innovating, improving, and competing in a rapidly changing environment if they maintain knowledge properly. Unfortunately, rational individuals tend only to participate in knowledge transfer if the costs needed is well compensated both internally or externally. Incentive is one of the external drives that companies usually apply to stimulate knowledge transfer. This research aims to analyze the effects of incentive mechanisms on knowledge transfer activities using agent-based model approach. Based on the interaction among agents, we construct a knowledge transfer network. The result suggests that incentive mechanism positively correlated with knowledge transfer efficiency. However, the effect is not significant to change the network structure.

articleTitle: On the Prediction of Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) stands as a prevalent endocrine disorder with a far-reaching impact on women and girls globally. Its effects span from skin pigmentation changes and hair loss, to potential infertility and the onset of mental health disorders such as anxiety and depression. The widespread occurrence of PCOS and the severity of its consequences reinforces the urgent need to address this medical condition. Present methods for accurately diagnosing PCOS can be costly and inconclusive. This challenge has driven the research presented in this paper, which aims to incorporate data science techniques into the PCOS diagnostic process in the hopes of developing a more rigorous and less subjective method for diagnosing the syndrome. We introduce, and illustrate the performance of, a new classification algorithm for the problem.

articleTitle: The Total Cost Of Ownership Of A Cold-Chain Vaccine Carrier Technology In Last-Mile Delivery: A Scoping Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) is a calculation used to illustrate the actual cost of buying and owning products and services. In this paper, we perform a scoping review aimed at understanding the TCO of technologies introduced in the last mile of the cold chain. The search is performed in Scopus, where the literature explored lies at the intersection of TCO models and frameworks, products service systems (PSS), and supply chain, value chain, or logistics application. We deliberately scoped broadly and refine towards PSS applications. We present the results of 20 publications meeting our inclusion criteria. The literature is largely produced by developed country authors, with a complete absence of African authors. A broad range of PSS were investigated, including airlines, telecommunications, commercial vehicles, tinting, machine tooling, electric and fuel vehicles for logistics and last-mile delivery, washing machines, renewable energy alternatives, and smallholder farming. Most of the publications developed TCO models for supplier selection, based on cost and other factors such as risk and reliability. Some developments focused on developing their TCO model beyond a cost calculator, and make contributions as decision support tools, negotiation tools, organizational tool, and a way to measure social impact. The scoping reviewed allowed us to identify activity-based cost categories to consider over the value chain of technologies introduced in the last mile of the cold chain.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Application Identification and Selection in Technology Push Models: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Technological innovation is becoming increasingly important to effectively address global change and the challenges it poses. The successful commercialisation of new technologies developed in university research is an essential component. University spin-offs (USOs) have considerable potential, particularly in creating disruptive innovations. Studies have shown that the initial development phase, in particular the identification and selection of applications, is crucial for the subsequent success of these spin-offs. Yet this is also a neglected area of research. To address this, this paper examines current theoretical models to assess the importance of this stage and derive implications for the primary phase of USOs, with the aim of providing optimal support for their journey towards successful commercialisation.

articleTitle: Exploring data-driven model-based systems engineering: a systematic literature review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
